title: The Takeout Paradox
editorialNotes: $40, $22, 19.1% and 30% figures are script copy with a BLS or EPA tie only for $56/week and 19.1%; none is hero type.

thread.element: receipt tape growing one cost line per slide

copy.headline: You ordered DoorDash because "there's nothing to eat."
copy.body: There was $40 of food in your fridge.

copy.headline: The average American household wastes $56/week in food.
items: That's not food you couldn't afford.
It's food you already paid for and then replaced with a $22 delivery order.

copy.headline: The fridge isn't empty. It's disorganized.
copy.body: You can't see what you have, so your brain defaults to "nothing good" and your thumb opens an app.

copy.headline: Inflation raised grocery prices 19.1% over 4 years.
items: You're paying more for the food AND throwing 30% of it away.
copy.citation: BLS Consumer Price Index food data, 2020–2024

copy.headline: Three costs stacking on top of each other:
items: the groceries you wasted + the delivery fee + the markup on the restaurant food.
One meal just cost you triple.

copy.headline: The most expensive meal is the one you already paid for and forgot about.
